Consumer sentiment declined in September, according to the University of Michigan’s monthly survey, but the mood improved from the survey’s preliminary reading.

The survey’s headline index landed at 48.1, versus 47.8 in its initial September reading published earlier this month. That was still a decline from August, when the reading was 51.7.

results.content: Annual inflation in the euro zone rose to 3.8% in September, beating market expectations to hit its highest level since September 2023. Last month's print is up from the 3.2% recorded in August, above the 3.6% forecast by markets and well ahead of the European Central Bank's 2% target. Core inflation came in at 2.5%, in line with expectations. The move was fueled by soaring energy prices caused by the ongoing Middle East conflict. This is a developing story.
results.title: Eurozone inflation hits its highest level in three years at 3.8% - CNBC

results.content: Social Security beneficiaries are expected to see a larger cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in 2027 than they received for this year, according to new estimates that follow the release of August inflation data. By law, the annual Social Security COLA is calculated using the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ consumer price index (CPI) inflation data for the months of July, August and September based on a variant of the dataset known as CPI-W. The BLS released the August CPI inflation data that showed consumer prices were up 3.4% from a year ago, while the CPI-W was up 3.5% over the last year. results.content: Gold prices eased on Wednesday as investors weighed the prospect of major central banks keeping interest rates elevated for longer in their efforts to curb persistent inflation. Spot gold fell 0.2% to $4,345.99 per ounce, as of 0147 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery were up 0.2% at $4,382.70. While bullion is often seen as a safeguard against inflation, its appeal tends to wane when elevated rates boost returns on interest-bearing investments. Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins wrote in a Linkedin post that she supported the U.S. central bank's decision last week to raise interest rates in the face of risks that future inflation will be above the 2% target.
